newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine soccer hooligan in murder trial.
newsitem.headline: Argentine soccer hooligan in murder trial.

text.p: Argentina's most notorious soccer hooligan went on trial on Friday in connection with the ambush and murder of two fans of a rival club in 1994, the state-run Telam news agency reported.
Jose Barrita, known by his nickname "The Grandfather", is accused of heading an illegal organisation of hooligan supporters of Buenos Aires club Boca Juniors who carried out the murder.

Police launched a big security operation around the Buenos Aires courtroom where Barrita and eight of his alleged underlings -- who, unlike their alleged chief, are accused of actively participating in the killings -- were taken to be tried.
A truckload of fans of the River Plate team were ambushed by pistol-toting Boca hooligans after a match between the two teams in April 1994.
One River supporter was shot dead, another fell out of the truck and was run over, and three received serious bullet wounds.
Barrita's lawyer Armando Murature said his client was innocent of all charges. Barrita is also accused of extorting money from Boca.
"He is a businessman who works with his mother and he can show how he made his income," Murature said.
Eleven Boca fans were sought by police over the shooting. One is on the run and another, nicknamed "Darling", died in prison of AIDS before the trial began.
